title: Hinduism: beliefs and practices
examples: Do Hindus believe in one God or many?
What happens at a Hindu temple?

explain.say: Hinduism grew up in South Asia over more than 3,000 years and has no single founder. Many Hindus call it Sanatana Dharma, the eternal way, and today about 1.2 billion people follow it, mostly in India and Nepal.

draw.label: Holy cities of India, many on the river Ganges

explain.say: Many Hindus believe in Brahman, one ultimate reality behind everything. The many deities, like Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess Devi, are often understood as forms or faces of that one divine reality.

items: Vishnu: the preserver, who comes as Rama and Krishna
Shiva: who destroys so things can renew
Devi: the Goddess, as Durga, Lakshmi, Saraswati

draw.text: Vaishnava, Shaiva and Shakta traditions focus on Vishnu, Shiva or the Goddess

explain.say: Four big ideas guide Hindu life. Dharma is doing your duty and what is right, karma is that actions have results, samsara is the cycle of birth and rebirth, and moksha is freedom from that cycle.

items: Dharma: duty, the right way to live

explain.say: Puja is Hindu worship. At home or in a mandir, people offer flowers, food and light to a murti, a sacred image of a deity, and wave a lamp in a ceremony called aarti.

draw.text: A mandir is a Hindu temple

explain.say: Hindu wisdom is kept in many sacred texts: the ancient Vedas and Upanishads, and the great epics, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, which contains the Bhagavad Gita.

items: from about 1500 BCE: the Vedas are composed
about 400 BCE to 400 CE: Mahabharata and Ramayana take shape
within the Mahabharata: the Bhagavad Gita

explain.say: Festivals fill the Hindu year with colour. Diwali celebrates light over darkness, Holi welcomes spring with coloured powder, and Navaratri honours the Goddess over nine nights.

draw.a: Light, colour and devotion through the year

faq.a: Dharma means duty, right action and the natural order that holds life together. For Hindus it means living rightly for your stage of life, like a student studying, a parent caring for family, and everyone being truthful and kind.

faq.q: Do Hindus believe in one God or many?
faq.a: Both answers can be heard. Many Hindus believe in one ultimate reality, Brahman, and see the many deities as its forms. Others devote themselves mainly to one deity, such as Vishnu, Shiva or the Goddess. Hinduism welcomes many views.
asks: How many gods do Hindus have?
Why do Hindus have so many gods?

faq.a: Hinduism has no single founder. It grew over thousands of years from the traditions of ancient India, including the Vedic hymns, and many teachers and sages shaped it.
Karma means action. Hindus believe good and harmful actions bring matching results, in this life or a future one, so your choices shape what comes next.
asks: What does karma mean for Hindus?

faq.a: Moksha is liberation, freedom from the cycle of birth, death and rebirth. Hindus describe it as realising the true self, the atman, and its unity with Brahman, or as eternal closeness to God, depending on the tradition.
asks: What is the goal of Hinduism?

faq.q: What happens at a Hindu temple?
faq.a: At a mandir people remove their shoes, ring a bell, and offer flowers, fruit or incense to the murti of the deity. Priests perform aarti, waving a lamp, and worshippers receive prasad, food that has been blessed.
asks: What do Hindus do at the mandir?

faq.a: Puja is Hindu worship, at home or in a temple. It usually includes prayers, offering flowers, food, water and light to a deity, and a lamp ceremony called aarti. Many Hindu homes have a small shrine for daily puja.

faq.q: What are the main Hindu holy books?
faq.a: The oldest are the Vedas, with the Upanishads that explore the self and Brahman. Much loved too are the epics, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, and the Bhagavad Gita, a conversation between Krishna and the warrior Arjuna.
asks: What is the Hindu holy book?

faq.q: Who are Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva?
faq.a: They are often called the Trimurti: Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver, and Shiva, who destroys so that the world can be renewed. Vishnu is believed to come to Earth as avatars such as Rama and Krishna.

faq.q: Why do many Hindus not eat beef?
faq.a: Many Hindus honour the cow as a gentle, giving animal, a symbol of life and generosity, so they do not eat beef. Many Hindus are vegetarian because of ahimsa, non-violence, though diets vary.
asks: Why is the cow sacred in Hinduism?

faq.a: Diwali is the festival of lights, usually in October or November. Hindus light diya lamps, set off fireworks, share sweets and worship Lakshmi. Many remember Rama returning home to Ayodhya, and the victory of light over darkness.
asks: What is the festival of lights?

faq.a: Om, or Aum, is a sacred sound and symbol in Hinduism. It is chanted at the start of prayers and is said to represent Brahman, the ultimate reality. It is also used in Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism in related ways.

Varanasi, on the river Ganges, is one of the holiest cities for Hindus and is sacred to Shiva. Pilgrims bathe in the Ganges, which Hindus revere as the goddess Ganga, and many hope to have their last rites there.
asks: Why do Hindus bathe in the Ganges?

facts: Hinduism has no single founder; many Hindus call it Sanatana Dharma, the eternal way.
About 1.2 billion people, about 15 percent of the world, were Hindu in 2020 (Pew Research).
The four aims of life in Hinduism are dharma, artha, kama and moksha.
The Bhagavad Gita is part of the epic Mahabharata.
Diwali, the festival of lights, usually falls in October or November.

quiz.show: Freedom from rebirth in Hinduism is…
quiz.why: Moksha means liberation, freedom from samsara, the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

wrong.0: Dharma is duty and right action.

quiz.say: A student studies hard and helps at home because it is right for her stage of life. Which Hindu idea is she following?
quiz.show: Doing your duty for your stage of life is…
quiz.why: Dharma is doing what is right and fitting for your role and stage of life.

wrong.0: Samsara is the cycle of rebirth, not a duty.
wrong.1: Aarti is the lamp ceremony in worship.
wrong.3: Prasad is blessed food given after worship.
